sources.entry: SIAM.AI GPU Watch - Menu bar app for monitoring NVIDIA GPUs across remote servers over SSH. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/siamaicorp/GPUWatch) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: A macOS menu bar app that monitors NVIDIA and AMD GPUs across remote servers over SSH, showing counts, temperature, utilisation and VRAM for multiple hosts in one panel.
keywords: see gpu temps on remote machines
summary.what_it_does: The app runs as a menu bar item on macOS 14 or later and polls configured hosts over the system's /usr/bin/ssh, using the user's existing ~/.ssh/config and keys. On each host it runs a fixed nvidia-smi query, or a rocm-smi query for AMD, and parses the result. It shows per-GPU status, temperature, utilisation, memory usage, and power where the driver reports it. Users can save GPU UUIDs as a baseline to flag missing or replacement cards, set optional per-host thresholds for temperature, VRAM and power, and enable notifications. A demo mode with simulated data is included, and the app stores its configuration and last-known readings locally.
use_cases: monitor GPU temperature and usage on several remote servers from a Mac menu bar
check whether a GPU server lost or swapped a card
watch AMD Instinct or ROCm hosts alongside NVIDIA machines
get alerts when a remote GPU overheats or its VRAM fills up
quick status glance at a lab or homelab GPU fleet
how_to_run: UNIVERSAL=1 ./Scripts/build-app.sh  (optional: universal Apple Silicon and Intel build)
notable: Agentless: uses the server's existing SSH service, with no monitoring agent to install on remote hosts
Handles both NVIDIA and AMD hosts, detecting the vendor automatically and reporting both on the same panel
Baseline tracking by GPU UUID, so a card replacement or index change after reboot can be identified
Separates SSH connectivity, GPU query results and data freshness, so an unreachable host is not reported as a missing GPU
Has no third-party dependencies and can be built from source with a single script
caveats: The downloadable build is ad-hoc signed and not notarised, so macOS Gatekeeper needs a quarantine flag cleared before it will open
Verified only on macOS 27.2.1 with Apple Silicon per the README; macOS 14-26 and Intel are stated as not verified, and csh/tcsh remote shells are not supported
AMD support covers rocm-smi only; ROCm 7's amd-smi is not supported, and some consumer AMD cards report a zero GUID so they cannot be tracked across reboots
